newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks inch up at close, see-saw session.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks inch up at close, see-saw session.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed slightly up in a late spurt after a session marked alternately by profit-taking and the Dow Jones, traders said.
"The market was very odd today, everybody was watching their positions. At times, we were up on the Dow's coattails, and then profit-takers stepped in," said a trader at the GBM brokerage.

The blue chip IPC index closed up 4.43 points, or 0.14 percent, at 3,290.38. Volume was moderate at 92.6 million shares traded. The Dow Jones closed up 96.53 points, or 1.59 percent, at a record 6,177.71.

Some dealers said they felt the late gain in the bourse was artificially produced by a large institution stepping in to buy stocks. The IPC had reached a session low just 20 minutes prior to the close.
One analyst, however, said that improved volume suggested an advance towards resistance at 3,300 points.
"The market had to improve after the U.S. election results. We're optimistic, we think it will keep climbing and that this (see-sawing) is temporary," said Daniel Romo, analyst at the Bancrecer bank.
On the broad market scoreboard, a total of 104 stocks changed hands, of which gainers outnumbered losers by 47 to 44.
Publishers Gfesa headed the gainers, up 20 centavos to 2.25 pesos, followed by retail stock Gigante, which closed 16 centavos up at 2.28 pesos.
Debt-stricken holding company Sidek headed the losers, down 70 centavos at 2.00 pesos, followed by its tourist arm Situr, down 11 centavos to 70 cetavos.
"Sidek and Situr don't look good and the market is hitting them," said a trader.
